author: microscope_agent

numbers.name: nosepiece_position
numbers.note: The person read the objective at the stand on 2026-09-24: the 20x dry, MRD70270, at position 2 of a turret indexed from 0. Stated so objective_clearance_min resolves from that lens's working distance, 0.8 mm; this plan commands no Z and no turret, and the stand is not moved.

operation.verifies: How closely the piezo X axis follows a host-timed sine of 290 um about 300 um at 1 Hz: the measured position against the commanded position at every point, over five cycles, as a position-against-time record. It also confirms that controller channel 1 moves the stage along X, by the image moving along X while it runs.
operation.falsified_by: the read-back after the approach or the return differs from its target by more than 1 um, or the image moves along Y or does not move while channel 1 is driven

stop_criteria.statement: stop, before the next move, if a read-back after a move differs from its target by more than 1 um

success_criteria.statement: the approach and the return each read back within 1 um, all 1000 sine points are sent and read, and the image moves along X

open_risks: PEAK SPEED about 1.8 mm/s (2 pi x 290 um x 1 Hz). No envelope limit bounds a piezo's speed, and it is about 29 times the fastest this stage was driven in the prior project; the person was told so in words and chose 1 Hz on 2026-09-24. How closely the stage tracks at that speed is what this run measures, and a sample on the stage is shaken across 580 um once a second.
Points 5 ms apart; the largest step between consecutive points is 9.1 um. A point sent more than one interval late is logged as late and never re-timed.
The sine starts at its minimum, 10 um, so the approach from the stage's rest (x = 0.025 um in run-20260924-004) is a 10 um step, not a 300 um one.
The return target is 0.5 um, not the rest position 0.025 um, so a read-back a few nanometres low cannot put the axis below the person's 0 um floor and leave the next command refused.
Piezo Z is not commanded: it rests 1.7 nm below the person's 0 um floor, and its direction toward the objective is unmeasured.
The channel-to-axis mapping (1 = x) is the person's statement and the controller's own label; the run watches the image to confirm it.

The objective in the path is the 20x dry at position 2, as the person read it at the stand; objective_clearance_min resolves to its 0.8 mm working distance. Nothing in this plan moves toward the objective.
